A remote adhesive monitoring system is used in conjunction with adhesive applied to workpieces moving along a production line. A reservoir, pump, and applicator dispense the adhesive onto the workpieces. A monitor control computer includes an associated data processing program. A pump cycle sensor detects pump cycles, an applicator sensor detects when adhesive is applied to the workpieces, and a workpiece sensor detects the workpieces moving along the line.

Using input from the applicator sensor and the workpiece sensor, the monitor control determines an ON time for each workpiece at a predetermined speed. Using input from the workpiece sensor and the pump cycle sensor, the monitor control determines the number of workpieces per pump cycle. The monitor control then calculates an ON-time-to-total-time ratio for each workpiece and, based on that ratio, calculates the amount of adhesive used.

A remote system for monitoring adhesive use operates with adhesive being dispensed onto workpieces as they travel along a production line. The adhesive is supplied and applied by a reservoir, a pump, and an applicator. A monitoring control computer, equipped with a related data processing program, oversees the process. A pump cycle sensor detects the operating cycles of the pump. An applicator sensor identifies the times when adhesive is delivered to the workpieces. A workpiece sensor detects the workpieces as they move through the line.

Using signals from the applicator sensor and the workpiece sensor, the monitoring control determines the adhesive application ON time for each workpiece at a preset speed. Using information from the workpiece sensor together with the pump cycle sensor, the monitoring control also determines how many workpieces correspond to each pump cycle. The system then computes, for each workpiece, the ratio of adhesive ON time to total time. Based on that ON-time-to-total-time ratio, the monitoring control calculates the quantity of adhesive consumed.
outputs.L3:
A remote adhesive monitoring system is used to track and evaluate the application of adhesive to workpieces as they move along a production line. The system is designed to monitor whether adhesive is being applied properly, how long the adhesive applicator remains active for each workpiece, and how much adhesive is consumed during production.

The system includes an adhesive reservoir, a pump, an adhesive applicator, a monitor control computer, and several sensors. The reservoir stores the adhesive material, while the pump delivers adhesive from the reservoir to the applicator. The applicator applies the adhesive to each workpiece as it passes through the application station. The monitor control computer receives and processes signals from sensors associated with the pump, the applicator, and the movement of the workpieces.

A pump cycle sensor detects the operating cycles of the adhesive pump. An applicator activity sensor detects when the applicator is turned on and applying adhesive. A workpiece movement sensor detects the presence or movement of each workpiece along the production line. These sensor inputs allow the monitor control computer to associate adhesive application activity with individual workpieces.

Using signals from the applicator activity sensor and the workpiece movement sensor, the monitor control determines the adhesive ON time for each workpiece. This ON time represents the period during which adhesive is actually being applied to a particular workpiece. The determination is made based on the known or predetermined speed of the workpieces moving along the production line, allowing the system to relate applicator activity to the position and timing of each workpiece.

The monitor control also uses signals from the workpiece movement sensor and the pump cycle sensor to determine how many workpieces are processed during each pump cycle. By correlating pump operation with the detected passage of workpieces, the system can estimate adhesive usage over a defined number of workpieces or production intervals.

For each workpiece, the monitor control calculates a ratio of adhesive ON time to TOTAL time. The TOTAL time may correspond to the time associated with the passage or processing of the workpiece at the predetermined production speed. This ON-time-to-total-time ratio indicates the portion of the workpiece processing interval during which adhesive was being applied.

The monitor control then uses this ratio to determine the amount of adhesive consumed for each workpiece. By combining the ON time information, pump cycle data, and workpiece count, the system can provide a remote indication of adhesive consumption and application performance. This enables operators or supervisors to monitor adhesive usage, detect irregularities, and verify that adhesive is being applied consistently across the production line.
outputs.L4:
A remote adhesive monitoring system is used to observe and measure the application of adhesive to workpieces as they move along a production line. The system is arranged so that adhesive usage can be tracked without requiring constant manual inspection of the applicator or the finished product. It includes sensors associated with the adhesive supply pump, the adhesive applicator, and the conveyor or other mechanism that moves the workpieces through the production area. These sensors generate signals that indicate when the pump completes a cycle, when the applicator is active, and when individual workpieces are present or moving through the adhesive application station.

The signals from these sensors are transmitted to a control computer or other processing unit. The control computer receives and analyzes the information in real time or over selected monitoring intervals. By processing the pump-cycle signal, the system can determine how often adhesive is being supplied to the applicator. By processing the applicator signal, it can determine the amount of time during which adhesive is actually being applied. By processing the workpiece movement signal, the system can determine how many workpieces pass through the station during a particular period or during a particular number of pump cycles.

Using this data, the system calculates several operating values that are useful for monitoring adhesive consumption. One value is the total ON time of the applicator, which represents the amount of time the adhesive applicator is activated. Another value is the number of workpieces processed per pump cycle, which helps indicate how much adhesive is being used relative to production output. A further value is the ratio of applicator ON time to total elapsed time, which provides a duty-cycle measurement for the adhesive application process.

From these calculated values, the system can estimate or determine adhesive usage with improved accuracy. Because the monitoring is based on actual production activity and actual applicator operation, the system can identify changes in adhesive consumption, detect abnormal operating conditions, and provide information that may be used to adjust the adhesive application process. For example, the system may reveal excessive adhesive use, insufficient adhesive application, irregular pump operation, or changes in production rate that affect consumption.

The monitored information may be displayed locally, transmitted to a remote location, stored for later analysis, or used to generate alarms or reports. In this way, the system enables accurate monitoring and control of adhesive consumption across a production line. It helps reduce waste, improve product quality, maintain consistent application, and provide production personnel with reliable data concerning the performance of the adhesive application equipment.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the following patent claim in plain English: a remote adhesive monitoring system with a reservoir, pump, applicator, pump cycle sensor, applicator sensor, workpiece sensor, and monitor control computer that calculates adhesive usage based on ON time/TOTAL time ratio and workpieces per pump cycle.
counterfactuals.output:
A remote adhesive monitoring system tracks how much adhesive is being used in an automated application process.

In plain English, it includes:

- A container holding the adhesive
- A pump that sends adhesive from the container to an applicator
- An applicator that applies adhesive to products or workpieces
- Sensors that detect:
  - when the pump cycles,
  - when the applicator is turned on,
  - and when each workpiece is present
- A control computer, located remotely, that receives the sensor information

The computer calculates adhesive usage by looking at how long the applicator is ON compared with the total operating time, and by determining how many workpieces are processed for each pump cycle. This allows the system to monitor adhesive consumption and application performance remotely.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an abstract for a patent describing a production-line adhesive monitoring system that senses pump cycles, applicator activation, and workpiece movement to calculate adhesive consumption per workpiece.
counterfactuals.output: An adhesive monitoring system for a production line is disclosed. The system includes one or more sensors configured to detect operating cycles of an adhesive supply pump, activation events of an adhesive applicator, and movement of workpieces along the production line. A controller receives signals from the sensors and correlates pump cycle data, applicator activation data, and workpiece movement data to determine adhesive usage attributable to individual workpieces or selected groups of workpieces. The controller may calculate adhesive consumption based on a calibrated adhesive volume per pump cycle and may compare calculated consumption values with predetermined thresholds to identify under-application, over-application, supply interruptions, applicator faults, or other process deviations. The system may generate alerts, store production and consumption records, and provide output to an operator interface or line control system, thereby enabling real-time monitoring of adhesive application quality and material usage without requiring direct measurement of adhesive flow at the applicator.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a concise technical description of an adhesive dispensing monitoring system where sensors track pump cycles, adhesive application events, and workpieces on a line, and a computer determines adhesive usage from ON-time ratios.
counterfactuals.output: An adhesive dispensing monitoring system uses sensors to track pump cycles, adhesive application events, and workpieces moving along a production line. Pump-operation sensors detect cycle counts or run states, applicator sensors detect adhesive ON/OFF events, and line sensors identify each workpiece or production interval. A computer receives these signals, correlates them by time or workpiece, and calculates adhesive usage based on the ratio of adhesive ON-time to total pump or production time. The system can estimate adhesive consumption per workpiece, compare usage against expected values, and generate alarms or reports for abnormal dispensing, missed applications, or excessive adhesive use.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert this invention into a patent-style summary: adhesive is applied to moving workpieces by a reservoir, pump, and applicator; sensors monitor pump cycles, applicator ON time, and workpiece presence; a control computer calculates adhesive used per workpiece.
counterfactuals.output:
A system for monitoring adhesive consumption during application to moving workpieces includes an adhesive reservoir, a pump configured to deliver adhesive from the reservoir, and an applicator configured to dispense the adhesive onto workpieces moving relative to the applicator. One or more sensors are operatively associated with the pump, the applicator, and a workpiece detection location to generate signals indicative of pump operating cycles, applicator ON-time, and the presence of individual workpieces.

A control computer receives the sensor signals and determines an amount of adhesive dispensed. The control computer correlates the determined adhesive usage with detected workpieces to calculate adhesive consumption on a per-workpiece basis. In some embodiments, the control computer determines adhesive usage based at least in part on a known or calibrated pump output per cycle, the number of pump cycles, and/or the duration for which the applicator is actuated. The system may thereby provide monitoring, reporting, or control of adhesive usage for each workpiece processed by the adhesive application system.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for a remote monitoring system used with adhesive applicators on a production line, including calculation of ON time per workpiece, workpieces per pump cycle, ON-to-total time ratio, and adhesive amount used.
counterfactuals.output: A remote monitoring system for adhesive applicators on a production line includes one or more adhesive dispensing applicators, a pump supplying adhesive to the applicators, sensors configured to detect applicator actuation, workpiece passage, and pump cycling, and a controller communicatively coupled to a remote monitoring device or server. The controller receives signals representative of adhesive ON time, total production time, workpiece count, and pump cycle count, and processes the signals to determine operating metrics for the adhesive application process. The metrics include ON time per workpiece, the number of workpieces processed per pump cycle, an ON-to-total time ratio for each applicator or production interval, and an estimated amount of adhesive used based on pump displacement, pump cycles, applicator flow rate, or combinations thereof. The calculated metrics are transmitted to a remote interface for display, storage, diagnostics, maintenance planning, adhesive consumption tracking, and detection of abnormal operating conditions in the production line.
